input:
This executive summary considers a proposed heat-recovery retrofit
at a food plant and the question of whether the project should
proceed to a capital decision at this stage. Refrigeration at the
plant uses 2148 MWh of electricity per year, a substantial
proportion of the site's total consumption. According to the
equipment vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 17% of that
use, which works out at a derived saving of 365 MWh per year at
the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $455k. At
an electricity price of $0.1 per kWh, the derived annual saving
comes to $36k, and the derived simple payback is 12.6 years. Two
qualifications should be attached to these figures. The saving is
a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant, and
refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, even
though the load is seasonal in character, so that an annual figure
constructed without the peak month may misstate the saving that
the retrofit would actually deliver.

Against that background, the recommendation of this summary is
that a metered trial should be carried out on one of the three
refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken on the
retrofit, and that the plant engineer should own the trial. A
trial of this kind would replace the vendor's projection with a
measured saving for the line in question, so that the eventual
capital decision can rest on a figure obtained from the plant
itself rather than on a figure supplied by the vendor.
target:
A metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines should
precede any capital decision on the heat-recovery retrofit, and
the plant engineer owns the trial. The case for the retrofit rests
on a projection by the equipment vendor, not on a measurement at
this plant, and the projected saving is large enough to test
before it is trusted with capital.

Refrigeration uses 2148 MWh of electricity per year at the plant.
The vendor projects that the retrofit would save 17% of that use,
a derived saving of 365 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The
capital cost is $455k. At an electricity price of $0.1 per kWh,
the derived annual saving is $36k, and the derived simple payback
is 12.6 years. Refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not
modelled, and the load is seasonal, so an annual figure built
without the peak month may misstate the saving. A metered trial on
one line replaces the projection with a measured saving for that
line, measured against the line's own metered consumption before
the retrofit is fitted, and the capital decision then rests on a
figure from the plant rather than a figure from the vendor.
